emergency.title: Emergency mode is on
emergency.body: SYNCLET_SSO_EMERGENCY=1 is set: single sign-on is switched off and everyone can sign in with a password. Fix the settings below, then remove the variable and restart the server.

password.title: Password sign-in
password.hint: Administrators can always sign in with their password, also when this is off (at /login?local=1).
password.forUsersHint: Turn off to have users sign in only through single sign-on.

oidc.title: OpenID Connect
oidc.hint: Single sign-on with an identity provider such as Authentik, Keycloak, Authelia or Microsoft Entra ID.
oidc.enabledHint: Shows a sign-in button on the login page. Accounts are created on first sign-in.
oidc.noPublicUrl: Needs SYNCLET_PUBLIC_URL on the server for the redirect URI.
oidc.redirectHint: Register this address as the redirect (callback) URI of the Synclet client at your identity provider.
oidc.redirectMissing: No redirect URI: set SYNCLET_PUBLIC_URL to the address Synclet is reached at (e.g. https://files.example.com) and restart the server. OpenID Connect can't be turned on until then.
oidc.redirectCopyManual: The address couldn't be copied automatically. It's selected: press Ctrl+C (⌘C on a Mac).
oidc.issuerHint: The provider's base address; Synclet reads /.well-known/openid-configuration from it.
oidc.secretKeepHint: Stored encrypted and never shown again.
oidc.secretReplaceHint: The new secret replaces the stored one when you save.
oidc.secretRemoveHint: Only for public clients that don't use a secret.
oidc.secretHint: Leave empty for public clients. Stored encrypted and never shown again.
oidc.scopesHint: Separated by spaces; must include openid.
oidc.buttonLabelHint: Text of the sign-in button on the login page.
oidc.usernameClaimHint: Becomes the username and folder name of new accounts.
oidc.groupsClaimHint: Claim that lists the user's groups.
oidc.linkByEmailHint: A first sign-in with a verified email address that matches a local account signs in to that account.
oidc.linkByEmailWarning: Only turn this on if you trust the identity provider to verify email addresses. Anyone who can get a matching, verified address there takes over the Synclet account with that address, including administrator accounts.

forward.title: Auth proxy (forward-auth)
forward.hint: A reverse proxy in front of Synclet signs users in (e.g. Authelia, Authentik outpost, oauth2-proxy) and passes the user in request headers.
forward.warningTitle: Only behind a proxy that strips these headers
forward.warning: Synclet trusts the headers below from the trusted proxy addresses. Your proxy must remove these headers from every incoming client request and set them itself. Otherwise anyone can sign in as any user, including administrators, by sending the header.
forward.enabled: Sign in through the auth proxy
forward.enabledHint: Users who arrive with the user header from a trusted proxy are signed in automatically.
forward.trustedProxiesHint: Only the address Synclet receives the headers from directly: in the shipped setup the fixed IP of the Caddy container, e.g. 172.30.0.10/32 (see README), not the whole Docker network. Headers from any other address are ignored.

groups.allowedHint: Only members of these groups can sign in. Empty: everyone. Removing someone from a group only blocks new sign-ins; to end their access now, disable the user.
groups.emptyWarning: No allowed groups: anyone with an account at this identity provider can sign in and gets a Synclet account with its own folder. With a public provider (Google, Microsoft, GitLab.com, ...) that means anyone on the internet. Enter at least one allowed group unless that is what you want.
groups.adminHint: Members become administrators; others become users at their next sign-in.

lockout.title: Locked out?
lockout.emergency: If a broken setting keeps everyone from signing in, start the server with this environment variable. It switches single sign-on off and allows password sign-in for everyone:
lockout.reset: If no administrator knows a password, set a new one on the server. Without a password on standard input a random one is printed:
lockout.local: Administrators with a password can always use the password form at /login?local=1.
